description: Clone a public Sequenzy email gallery sequence into a draft sequence for this company, with the example's trigger family (signup, abandoned cart, order placed, or inactive tag) and send timing, up to 12 emails (the first 12 unless stepNumbers picks which; each kept email keeps its original timing from the trigger). AI then writes every email in the company's brand in the background (usually 30-60 seconds); poll get_sequence until enrichmentStatus is complete. If this tool returns enrichmentStatus not_queued with a warning, the draft exists but writing did not start: open it in the dashboard and do not call this tool again. The sequence stays a draft and sends nothing until enabled. Requires sequences:write. Each call creates another sequence. Accepts a gallery sequence URL (https://sequenzy.com/email-examples/brands/{brand}/sequences/{sequence}) or brand plus sequence slugs.

brand.description: Gallery brand slug from the URL (/email-examples/brands/{brand}/...). Use with the example slug instead of url.

brief.description: Optional direction, up to 1000 characters, such as an offer or feature to highlight. Takes priority over the example.

companyId.description: Company ID. If not provided, uses the currently selected company.

emailStyle.description: Generated email style. Defaults to the company's email style preference.

name.description: Optional name, up to 200 characters, for what is created.

sequence.description: Gallery sequence slug from the URL (/sequences/{sequence}). Use with brand instead of url.

stepNumbers.description: Optional: which of the example's emails to clone, as 1-based positions in the gallery sequence (Email 1, Email 2, ...), 1 to 12 distinct positions. Defaults to the first 12. These are positions in the example, not the stepNumber of the created sequence's steps.

url.description: Email gallery page URL. Provide either url, or brand plus the example slug; not both.

name: create_sequence_from_example

outputSchema.description: Structured content returned by the `create_sequence_from_example` MCP tool.

appUrls.description: Dashboard URLs for relevant Sequenzy resources.

example.description: The gallery sequence it was cloned from: brand, name, url, omittedEmailCount (the example's emails left out: not chosen in stepNumbers, or beyond the 12-step limit) and stepNumbers (positions of the cloned emails in the example).

items.description: Fallback array wrapper used only when a tool returns a bare array.

message.description: What was created and what happens next.

sequence.description: The sequence record returned by Sequenzy. Run state: branch on effectiveStatus (draft, live, enrollment_paused, paused, or archived) rather than on status, which reads `active` even when new enrollments are paused. acceptsNewEnrollments and processesExistingEnrollments answer the two questions behind it, and effectiveStatusSummary is a plain-language sentence. The legacy triggerConfig.active flag is not read by the runtime; it is reported as a mirror of acceptsNewEnrollments. Email numbering: emails[].stepNumber and nodes[].config.stepNumber are legacy stored ordinals retained for compatibility. Prefer emails[].structuralStepNumber and nodes[].structuralStepNumber when explaining the visible sequence position. Structural numbers are graph-derived; emails in parallel branches intentionally share a depth. Sequences use sendingWindow for allowed local hours/days; they do not have Send Time Optimization. frequencyCapEnabled is true when email steps respect the company frequency cap (get_frequency_cap): contacts already at the cap skip the step. activeSubscribersOnly is true when only active contacts enter; when false, unsubscribed and bounced contacts still enter and only their marketing emails are skipped. STO is per-campaign (list_campaigns / get_campaign sendTimeOptimization).

subscriptionUrl.description: Owner-facing subscription, upgrade, and billing-management URL when available.

url.description: Primary dashboard URL for this result.

value.description: Fallback object wrapper used only when a tool returns a non-object value.

warnings.description: Non-fatal cautions about content, permissions, or follow-up actions.
